statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains in the watch band and below the block threshold.
recommendation: Tail sits at 21% after an orderly recovery session that closed near its high with volatility decaying. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the Friday U.S. data block and cash open at 13:15-14:30 UTC; existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 recovers 1.73% after the Fed-day drop; volatility decays into a quarterly expiry Friday
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,446.98, up 1.73%, recovering the bulk of the decline that followed the Federal Reserve's 25 basis point increase to a 3.75%-4% target range on 16 September. The session traded a 29,305.90-29,494.95 cash range and finished near its high, with NQ futures holding the upper part of a 29,247.75-29,793.25 range. Cross-asset inputs aligned constructively: the 10-year Treasury yield eased back below 5% to roughly 4.93% after touching its highest level since 2007, WTI crude fell a second session toward $101 as Saudi Arabia moved to restore East-West pipeline capacity, and the VIX fell about 13% to 15.41. Breadth was broad rather than narrow, with semiconductors leading and megacap technology uniformly higher. That combination is a persistent one-way cash session, which is genuine Tail evidence, set against decaying volatility and orderly two-way price discovery, which is not. Tail is therefore held at 21% in the watch band rather than raised toward the block threshold. Stress stays elevated at 45% because the dot plot showed 16 of 18 officials projecting a further increase this year, the 10-year remains near 5%, and Gulf supply routes remain an unresolved headline channel. Today's U.S. releases printed firm, with initial jobless claims at 196,000 and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index at 37.8. The forecast path steps down through the low-liquidity overnight hours and rises again into Friday's 13:15 UTC Industrial Production release, the 13:30 UTC Bowman appearance and the U.S. cash open, then into the quarterly quadruple-witching settlement in the final hour of the window.

lookbackSummary: The 24 hours to 20:00 UTC are fully covered by published Claude assessments. Tail moved between 16% and 26%, peaking at 26% around the 13:00 UTC approach to the U.S. cash open and easing steadily to 20% by 19:00 UTC as the recovery proceeded in an orderly fashion. Stress fell monotonically from 75% at the Fed-day close to 46%, reflecting decaying volatility rather than a change in the policy outlook. The dominant mode was trend-up for most of the European and U.S. hours.
outlookSummary: The projected path steps down to the 17%-18% range through the CME maintenance halt and the thin overnight hours, then rises with participation across the European morning. It reaches a first conditional peak of 24% around 14:00 UTC on Friday, covering August Industrial Production at 13:15 UTC, the Bowman appearance at 13:30 UTC and the U.S. cash open into quarterly expiry, and a second 24% peak in the 19:00 UTC power hour ahead of the quadruple-witching settlement. No hour in the window is projected above the watch band, so no blocking state is projected. Stress is projected to ease toward 41% overnight and rebuild to roughly 51% into the expiry close. Confidence declines gradually with evidence age rather than with risk.
